newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-TASMANIA STILL IN DRIVING SEAT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TASMANIA STILL IN DRIVING SEAT.

text.p: Tasmania strengthened their bid for a place in the Sheffield Shield final despite their match against Queensland ending in a draw on Monday.

Tasmania, the favourites to face Western Australia in Perth later this month, consolidated second place in the Shield table by claiming two competition points for taking a first innings lead earlier in the four-day match at Bellerive Oval in Hobart.

Queensland captain Stuart Law, a regular member of Australia's limited overs side, remained unbeaten on 74 at close of play on Monday as Queensland reached 198 for four in pursuit of a victory target of 389 on the final day.
New South Wales and Queensland remain in the hunt with Tasmania to finish second behind Shield leaders Western Australia, who will host the five-day final at the WACA Ground.

The struggle will be settled next weekend when the final round of matches in the regular season will be played but a victory for Tasmania would guarantee them a final berth regardless of the results elsewhere.

Western Australia have 36 points from nine matches, an unassailable 10 points clear of Tasmania. Queensland and New South Wales are locked together on 22 points in third place. An outright victory is worth six points.
In the other match completed on Monday, South Australia beat Victoria by 161 runs fourth-placed Victoria at Adelaide Oval.
